senses.gloss: The highest point or level that something reaches.
examples: Ticket sales hit their *peak* in early June.
At its *peak*, the company employed four thousand people.
Traffic reaches a *peak* right around five o'clock.

senses.gloss: A very small amount of money, used in the plural.
examples: They pay their interns *peanuts*.
He sold the truck for *peanuts*.
A fine like that is *peanuts* to a company this size.

senses.gloss: A lever pushed with the foot to drive a bicycle or work a machine.
examples: She stood up on the *pedals* to get up the hill.
He slammed his foot on the brake *pedal*.
One *pedal* came off my bike on the way home.

senses.gloss: A small ball of metal fired from an air gun or a shotgun.
examples: The vet took three *pellets* out of the dog's shoulder.
A shotgun shell sprays dozens of tiny *pellets*.
The air rifle fires small lead *pellets*.

senses.gloss: A punishment given to a player or team for breaking a rule in a game.
examples: The *penalty* moved the ball back fifteen yards.
He sat two minutes in the box for a tripping *penalty*.
The referee called three *penalties* in the first half.

senses.gloss: An extra charge you have to pay for paying late or breaking the terms of an agreement.
examples: There's a *penalty* for taking the money out early.
Pay the bill by Friday to avoid a late *penalty*.
The contract has no *penalty* for canceling.

senses.gloss: A length of time with a beginning and an end.
examples: Sales were flat over a six-month *period*.
He went through a rough *period* after the divorce.
Rain is expected for short *periods* tomorrow afternoon.

senses.gloss: One of the parts a school day is divided into for classes.
examples: I have chemistry third *period*.
She grades papers during her free *period*.
The fire drill ate up most of second *period*.

senses.gloss: The monthly flow of blood from a woman's body.
examples: Her *period* is usually right on schedule.
The cramps are worst on the first day of my *period*.
She hasn't had a *period* since March.

senses.gloss: An annoying person who keeps bothering you.
examples: Stop being such a *pest* and let me finish this.
The kids next door are complete *pests*.
He made a *pest* of himself calling every hour.

senses.gloss: A person treated as a favorite by someone in charge.
examples: Everyone knew he was the teacher's *pet*.
She was always the boss's *pet*.
Being the coach's *pet* didn't win him any friends.

senses.gloss: A small flat piece of plastic used to pluck the strings of a guitar.
examples: He keeps a *pick* tucked under the strings.
I dropped my *pick* inside the guitar.
She plays with her fingers instead of a *pick*.

senses.gloss: A heavy tool with a pointed metal head, swung to break up rock or hard ground.
examples: The crew broke the frozen ground with *picks* and shovels.
He swung the *pick* into the packed clay.
A rusted miner's *pick* hung by the door.

senses.gloss: A pointed wooden stake used to build a fence.
examples: Two *pickets* had rotted at the base.
He painted every *picket* by hand.
The fence is made of pointed cedar *pickets*.

senses.gloss: A difficult or awkward situation.
examples: We're in a real *pickle* now that the car won't start.
His lie got him into quite a *pickle*.
She helped me out of a *pickle* last year.

senses.gloss: The act of collecting someone or something at an arranged time and place.
examples: Your order will be ready for *pickup* at noon.
Trash *pickup* is on Tuesday mornings.
School *pickup* is a madhouse at three o'clock.

senses.gloss: An increase or improvement in activity.
examples: Dealers reported a *pickup* in sales this spring.
Economists expect a *pickup* in hiring later this year.
There's been a nice *pickup* in traffic to the site.

senses.gloss: An easy or pleasant experience, almost always used in the negative.
senses.ru: лёгкое дело, приятное занятие (обычно с отрицанием)
examples: Recovering from the surgery was no *picnic*.
Two weeks with three toddlers is no *picnic*.
Moving in August was no *picnic*, believe me.

senses.gloss: The general situation, seen as a whole.
examples: The report gives a bleak *picture* of the housing market.
Try to keep the big *picture* in mind.
The new numbers change the whole *picture*.

senses.gloss: The image that appears on a television or a screen.
examples: The sound is fine but the *picture* keeps freezing.
Move the antenna until the *picture* clears up.
That old set still has a sharp *picture*.

senses.gloss: A movie.
examples: It won best *picture* at the awards that year.
He directed three *pictures* before he turned thirty.
The studio releases about a dozen *pictures* a year.

senses.gloss: The whole amount of money or benefit that is to be divided up.
examples: Every department wants a bigger slice of the *pie*.
Growing the *pie* helps everyone, he argued.
Streaming services took a large piece of the *pie*.

senses.gloss: A greedy, rude, or dirty person.
examples: Don't be a *pig* — leave some for your sister.
He eats like a *pig*.
Those guys left the kitchen like *pigs*.

senses.gloss: A very dirty or messy place.
examples: Clean your room — it's a *pigpen*.
The apartment was a *pigpen* the morning after the party.
His truck is a rolling *pigpen*.

senses.gloss: A person or idea that something important depends on.
examples: She was a *pillar* of the community for forty years.
Free speech is one of the *pillars* of democracy.
Trust is the *pillar* the whole business rests on.

senses.gloss: A small low concrete shelter with narrow slits for guns.
examples: Concrete *pillboxes* still line the beach.
The squad took fire from a *pillbox* on the ridge.
An abandoned *pillbox* sits at the edge of the field.

senses.gloss: A small trial version of a program, run to see whether it works.
examples: The district is running a *pilot* in four schools.
If the *pilot* goes well, they'll expand it statewide.
We tested the software in a six-week *pilot*.

senses.gloss: The first episode of a television series, made to test whether people will watch it.
examples: The network ordered a *pilot* but never picked up the show.
They shot the *pilot* last spring.
I watched the *pilot* and got hooked.

senses.gloss: Someone who steers a ship through a harbor or a difficult stretch of water.
examples: A *pilot* came aboard to guide the tanker into port.
The harbor *pilot* climbed a rope ladder up the hull.
River *pilots* know every sandbar by heart.

senses.gloss: A short tube with a bowl at one end, used for smoking tobacco.
examples: My grandfather smoked a *pipe* on the porch every evening.
He tapped the ash out of his *pipe*.
The shop sells *pipes* and loose tobacco.

senses.gloss: A tube that sounds a musical note when air passes through it.
examples: The church organ has over two thousand *pipes*.
The tallest *pipes* reach almost to the ceiling.
He played a simple tune on a wooden *pipe*.

senses.gloss: The pipes in a building or machine, taken together.
examples: The old copper *piping* has to be replaced.
*Piping* runs behind the wall to the water heater.
Rusted *piping* was leaking under the floor.

senses.gloss: Someone who illegally copies and sells films, music, or software.
examples: Software *pirates* had the game online within a day.
The studio sued a group of *pirates* overseas.
Video *pirates* filmed the movie from a theater seat.

senses.gloss: A deep hole dug in the ground.
examples: They dug a *pit* for the fire.
Gravel is hauled out of the *pit* all summer.
He nearly fell into an open *pit* at the construction site.

senses.gloss: The area beside a racetrack where cars stop for fuel and tires.
examples: He came into the *pits* on lap thirty.
The crew changed four tires in the *pit* in seven seconds.
A slow stop in the *pits* cost her the race.

senses.gloss: A speech meant to persuade someone to buy something or agree to a plan.
examples: The salesman gave us the whole *pitch* about the extended warranty.
She has ten minutes to make her *pitch* to investors.
I've heard that *pitch* before.

senses.gloss: A throw of the ball to the batter in baseball.
examples: He swung at the first *pitch*.
That fastball was the best *pitch* of the inning.
The umpire called the *pitch* a strike.

senses.gloss: The steepness of a slope, especially of a roof.
examples: The roof has a steep *pitch*, so the snow slides right off.
A low *pitch* makes the attic hard to stand up in.
Builders measure *pitch* in inches of rise per foot.

senses.gloss: Something that makes you feel disappointed or sorry.
examples: It's a *pity* you can't stay longer.
What a *pity* the museum is closed today.
It would be a *pity* to throw out perfectly good food.

senses.gloss: The house or apartment where someone lives.
examples: We're having dinner at my *place* tonight.
Her new *place* is a lot closer to work.
They're looking for a bigger *place* downtown.

senses.gloss: A seat or spot kept for a particular person.
examples: Save my *place* in line while I get coffee.
Set a *place* for your grandmother.
She took her *place* at the front of the room.

senses.gloss: The position someone finishes in a race or competition.
examples: She finished in second *place*.
Our team took last *place* again.
First *place* pays a thousand dollars.

senses.gloss: A drawing that shows a building or a room as seen from above.
examples: The architect emailed us the floor *plans*.
The *plan* shows where the outlets go.
They changed the *plans* to add a second bathroom.

senses.gloss: An arrangement with a company for a service you pay for regularly.
examples: My phone *plan* includes unlimited data.
The company offers a decent health *plan*.
We switched to a cheaper *plan* last month.

senses.gloss: One of the main points in a political party's program.
examples: Tax reform was the central *plank* of his campaign.
The party added a *plank* on climate change.
Both *planks* were dropped from the final platform.

senses.gloss: Someone whose job is to plan something such as a city, a wedding, or a budget.
examples: City *planners* want to widen the sidewalk.
We hired a wedding *planner* to handle the details.
A financial *planner* walked us through our retirement options.

senses.gloss: A factory or a building where power is produced or goods are made.
examples: The assembly *plant* employs two thousand people.
A power *plant* sits on the far side of the river.
The *plant* shuts down for two weeks every July.

senses.gloss: A person secretly placed in a group to spy on it or influence it.
examples: The heckler turned out to be a *plant*.
Police used a *plant* inside the gang.
Half the audience suspected the volunteer was a *plant*.

senses.gloss: A flat piece of metal or stone fixed to a wall with writing on it.
examples: A bronze *plaque* marks the spot where he was born.
They gave her a *plaque* for thirty years of service.
*Plaques* along the trail explain the local history.

senses.gloss: A fatty deposit that builds up on the inside of an artery.
examples: The scan showed *plaque* narrowing the artery.
These drugs can slow the buildup of *plaque*.
*Plaque* in the arteries raises the risk of a heart attack.

senses.gloss: The clear yellowish liquid part of blood that carries the cells.
examples: He donates *plasma* twice a month.
The lab spun the sample to separate the *plasma*.
Burn patients often need *plasma*.

senses.gloss: Activity done for fun, especially by children.
examples: Young children learn through *play*.
The yard gives them room for outdoor *play*.
It's all work and no *play* around here.

senses.gloss: A single action or planned move in a sports game.
examples: That catch was the best *play* of the game.
The coach drew up a *play* during the timeout.
They ran the same *play* three times in a row.

senses.gloss: A small amount of loose movement in a mechanical part.
examples: There's too much *play* in the steering wheel.
A little *play* in the chain is normal.
The hinge has some *play* now that the screws are loose.

senses.gloss: A machine or program that plays recorded sound or video.
examples: The DVD *player* won't read the disc.
He still keeps a record *player* in the den.
The video *player* on that site keeps buffering.

senses.gloss: A company or person that is active and important in a particular field.
examples: The startup became a major *player* in cloud storage.
Three big *players* control most of the market.
She's a serious *player* in state politics.

senses.gloss: An urgent emotional request for help.
examples: The family made a public *plea* for information.
He ignored her *pleas* to slow down.
The shelter issued a *plea* for winter coats.

senses.gloss: A secret plan by several people to do something harmful or illegal.
examples: Police uncovered a *plot* to rob the bank.
The *plot* against the mayor fell apart.
He went to prison for his part in the *plot*.

senses.gloss: A small marked-off piece of ground.
examples: They bought a *plot* of land outside town.
Each family tends its own *plot* in the community garden.
My grandparents bought burial *plots* years ago.

senses.gloss: A truck or blade that pushes snow off roads.
examples: The *plow* came through around four in the morning.
*Plows* were out all night on the interstate.
The *plow* left a wall of snow at the end of the driveway.

senses.gloss: A piece of rubber or metal that fits into a hole to block it.
examples: Pull the *plug* and let the tub drain.
The mechanic loosened the oil *plug*.
He hammered a rubber *plug* into the bottom of the boat.

senses.gloss: A short favorable mention of a product or event in public.
examples: She got in a quick *plug* for her new book.
Thanks for the *plug* on your show last night.
The whole interview was really just a *plug* for the movie.

senses.gloss: A large showy feather worn as decoration.
examples: The hat was trimmed with an ostrich *plume*.
White *plumes* nodded above the horses' heads.
A single *plume* stood up from his helmet.

senses.gloss: The part of a syringe or similar device that you push down.
examples: The nurse pressed the *plunger* slowly.
Push the *plunger* down to strain the coffee.
The *plunger* on the syringe was stuck.

senses.gloss: A small area or group that is different from everything around it.
examples: There are still *pockets* of snow on the north slope.
The census found *pockets* of deep poverty in the county.
We hit a *pocket* of rough air over the mountains.

senses.gloss: The money a person or group has available to spend.
examples: The repair came straight out of my own *pocket*.
The lawsuit was funded by donors with deep *pockets*.
Rising rents are hitting renters' *pockets* hard.
